problem_statement: A generic utility function is needed to count the number of set bits in a byte array of arbitrary length. The function should accept a pointer to a value and its size in bytes, and return the total number of set bits across all bytes. It should use a hardware popcount instruction when available, and otherwise fall back to a portable byte-by-bit algorithm. Several subsystems (Bluetooth audio, ADC driver, kernel bitarray tests) currently have their own local bit-counting implementations that should be replaced by this shared function.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p qemu_x86 -T tests/kernel/common -s tests/kernel/common/kernel.common -s kernel.common -O twister-out --no-clean -W
